study type: single arm proof of concept trial
exposure: Extended balloon labour induction (using 2-3 balloons side-by-side)
cohort: 20 pregnant women with a modified Bishop cervical score of 7 or more, deemed unsuitable for single balloon labour induction, at Princess Marina Hospital (PMH) in Gaborone, Botswana.
finding: The use of side-by-side balloons for extended labour induction/augmentation in women with a favorable cervix was effective in achieving vaginal birth in most participants without the need for uterotonics or amniotomy.
